findings.reason: Keeping only the latest reply reference can indefinitely delay a legitimate notification when an earlier queued reply remains readable and a later one is private; permission must be checked at send time, but no evidence requires a one-reference limit or rules out choosing among bounded, independently retained witnesses.

findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: The spec acknowledges a local save and lets a disconnected holder act on an older preference without requiring a signed all-member commitment or repair before serving a current view, so it does not meet the Conversations Pending exception.

An anonymous queue entry that may contain a critical notice can remain held indefinitely when recipient continuity cannot be proved, with no specified cadence to revisit the hold or reach a deliberate disposition.

findings.standard: Verify the State, Not Its Symbol
findings.reason: The proposed `deliverySupport` check measures whether active holders support typed queues, yet an older holder can create an anonymous summary after all queues were inspected empty, so `legacySummaryState:none` cannot justify omitting the older-summary warning while that holder remains active.

The opening leads with an unexplained Chief handoff, server card and frozen verification queue before describing current chat behavior, leaving a reader outside the project session to infer what those references mean.

fit.reason: The spec requires plain-language mute confirmations, but its core design governs preference storage, archive filtering, and notification delivery, leaving action placement and phone-width usability to the app.
